name: logo-cloud
description: "Trusted by" strip: a small muted eyebrow over a row of customer marks, each an set to one height, desaturated at rest and returning to colour under the pointer. Composition only: zero JavaScript, no controller, no reactive directives — the grid layout is a centred wrapping cluster, the marquee layout hands the items to the nested marquee primitive.

heading.description: The eyebrow ('Trusted by teams at'). A paragraph, not a heading, so the strip stays out of the document outline; give it an id and point the section's aria-labelledby at it so the landmark is named

items.description: The list of marks in the grid layout — a centred, wrapping cluster. Absent in the marquee layout, where the nested marquee's two [data-part='track'] lists take its place

item.description: One mark. A direct child of the items list, or of a marquee track; holds the logo as its direct child (or a link wrapping it — focus inside the item brings the colour back)

logo.description: The mark itself, an whose alt is the company name. Sized to --logo-cloud-height with its own width (object-fit: contain), greyscale and dimmed at rest unless data-color is set. In a marquee's aria-hidden second track the copies carry alt=''

color.description: Keep every mark in its own colours at rest instead of greyscale-and-dimmed; the hover return is then a no-op.

--logo-cloud-height.description: Height every mark is set to (custom property); widths follow each image's own ratio.

--logo-cloud-width.description: Widest a single mark may grow (custom property), so a long wordmark cannot dwarf the glyphs beside it.

--logo-cloud-dim.description: Opacity of a mark at rest, before the pointer brings it back to 1 (custom property). Ignored with data-color.

--logo-cloud-max.description: Maximum width of the grid layout's cluster before it wraps (custom property).

required_attrs: aria-labelledby on the section pointing at the heading id
alt text on every logo image naming the company (empty alt only on the copies in a marquee's aria-hidden second track)
in the marquee layout: role='group' and an aria-label on the nested marquee, and aria-hidden='true' on its second track
a11y.notes: The marks are a real list, so assistive technology announces how many there are. Greyscale is a visual treatment only — the accessible name of each mark is its alt text, unchanged by the filter. In the marquee layout the strip pauses on hover and on focus-within (the marquee's own behaviour) and, under reduced motion, becomes a wrapped row of each mark once. Keep links out of a marquee track; a link inside the hidden copy would be a second, unlabelled tab stop.

keyboard.Tab: move through any links wrapping the marks, in source order; a focused item shows its mark in colour

templates.html: {heading}
templates.html_marquee: {heading}

notes: In the marquee layout the <ul> elements are the MARQUEE's [data-part='track'] slots, not logo-cloud's; logo-cloud's own items part is absent. The items and logos inside the tracks are still logo-cloud's parts (the marquee declares neither), and the stylesheet reaches them through the track as an element, never as another component's part.
The two marquee tracks must be identical, down to the marks' order; only the alt text differs (empty on the hidden copy).

To let the strip arrive with the page, wrap the whole section in a data-ui='reveal' (data-variant='fade' is the calm choice), as the reference markup shows. The reveal is a wrapper around the pattern, not a part of it — a reveal must wrap, and the pattern's parts are its own.
Image sources in the reference markup are https://example.com placeholders; replace them with the marks, and keep the alt text as the company name.
